title: Best time to visit Sikkim and Darjeeling, month by month
meta_description: Month-by-month guide to Sikkim and Darjeeling weather, views, snow, crowds and road closures, with the best months for each kind of trip.
summary: The best months for Sikkim and Darjeeling are October and November for clear mountain views, and March to May for flowers and mild weather. December to February is cold but clear, with snow on the high roads. The monsoon, from mid-June to September, brings heavy rain, landslides and permit suspensions, though it is quiet and cheap.
key_takeaways: October and November give the clearest Kangchenjunga views of the year, but October is also the busiest month.
April and May bring rhododendrons at Yumthang and on the road to Tsomgo, with peak crowds and prices in May.
From mid-June to September the monsoon closes roads and suspends permits in North Sikkim, so keep that season for relaxed town stays.
Snow is most reliable from December to March at Tsomgo, Zero Point and Sandakphu, but it can also close those roads for days.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: There are two good seasons in the Eastern Himalaya and two harder ones. Autumn, from October to November, is the classic season: the monsoon has washed the air clean, the roads are open and Kangchenjunga stands clear above Gangtok and Darjeeling most mornings. Spring, from March to May, is warmer and greener, with rhododendrons and magnolias in flower, though haze often softens the views by afternoon.

Winter, from December to February, is cold but often brilliantly clear. Gangtok and Darjeeling rarely get snow, but Tsomgo Lake freezes, Zero Point and Sandakphu are white, and snow can close the high roads for days at a time. The monsoon, from mid-June to September, is the hard season. Rain is heavy, mountains vanish into cloud, and landslides block roads, especially NH10 along the Teesta.

The best month for you depends on what you want to see. The table and the notes below set out each month for Gangtok, Darjeeling and North Sikkim. Weather patterns shift from year to year, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Autumn: October and November
paras: If you can choose only one season, choose autumn. The views are the best of the year, with Kangchenjunga clear from Tashi viewpoint in Gangtok and from Tiger Hill above Darjeeling on most mornings. Roads in North Sikkim are at their most stable, and the Sandakphu trek reopens after the monsoon break.

October has one drawback: it is the busiest month of the year. Durga Puja, Dashain and Tihar fill the hills with holidaymakers from Kolkata and the rest of Bengal, and hotels, cars and toy train seats sell out weeks ahead. November is almost as clear, colder at night, and much quieter once the festival holidays end. For most travellers it is the single best month.
Nights at Zuluk and Lachen fall below freezing in November, so pack a warm jacket even if Gangtok feels mild by day.

sections.heading: Spring: March to May
paras: Spring is the flower season. Rhododendrons start flowering lower down in March and reach Yumthang valley from mid-April, with the Shingba rhododendron sanctuary at its best in late April and May. The road to Tsomgo is lined with blooms, and the Singalila ridge to Sandakphu is one of the finest spring walks in the Himalaya. First-flush Darjeeling tea is plucked in March and second flush begins in May.

The trade-off is visibility. Haze builds as the weeks go by and afternoon clouds often hide the mountains, so plan viewpoints for early morning. May is also peak holiday season for Indian families, with full hotels in Gangtok, crowds at Tsomgo and higher prices everywhere. March and early April give much of the spring at lower cost.

sections.heading: Winter: December to February
paras: Winter is cold, dry and often very clear. January gives the best chance of a clean view of Kangchenjunga from Darjeeling, and hotel prices are low outside the Christmas and New Year week. Snow is rare in Gangtok and Darjeeling towns but likely at Tsomgo, Zero Point, Lachung and Sandakphu. Families from the plains often come for exactly that.

The catch is access. Heavy snow closes the road to Nathu La, above Zuluk and to Gurudongmar for days at a time, and the Gurudongmar road is often shut after big falls in January and February. Treat any high destination as a bonus rather than a promise, and keep a spare day. Festivals help fill the gaps: Losoong and the Kagyed Chaam bring masked dances to Gangtok in December, and Losar falls in February or early March.

sections.heading: Monsoon: June to September
paras: The monsoon usually arrives in early to mid-June and stays until late September. July is the wettest month. Mountains are hidden for days, landslides block NH10 and the hill roads, and North Sikkim permits are often suspended during heavy rain. Since the October 2023 flood in the Teesta valley, some stretches of road are temporary and more fragile in the rains. The national parks of the Dooars close from 16 June to 15 September, and Neora Valley near Lava closes from about mid-June to mid-September.

Still, the monsoon has its fans. Tea gardens are deep green, Darjeeling hotels are at their cheapest in August, and towns are quiet. Pang Lhabsol brings masked dances to Gangtok in late August or September. If you travel now, stay low, keep plans flexible and avoid permit areas. Kalimpong villages and Dzongu are safer bets than the high valleys. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Holidays, crowds and booking ahead
paras: Weather is only half the story. The Eastern Himalaya is the nearest mountain holiday for much of eastern India, so school and festival holidays shape prices and availability as much as the season does. The busiest weeks are the Durga Puja and Diwali holidays in October, the Christmas and New Year week, and the summer school holidays from mid-May to early June.

In those weeks, hotels in Gangtok and Darjeeling fill early, registered vehicles for Tsomgo and North Sikkim run short, and toy train seats sell out. Book rooms and cars four to six weeks ahead, and expect higher rates. Shared jeeps from Siliguri also fill fast in the mornings, so start early.

Outside these weeks you can be much more relaxed. In March and November we can often confirm a North Sikkim trip a few days ahead at better rates, and walk-in rooms are easy to find in Pelling, Kalimpong and Darjeeling. Late January and February, outside Losar, are quieter still.

Whatever the month, build one spare day into any trip that includes a permit area or a long mountain drive. Weather in the hills changes fast, and a spare day turns a closed road into a minor delay rather than a missed train or flight.

sections.heading: Best months for each kind of trip
paras: Use this list as a starting point. Every month has its trade-offs, and the right choice depends on whether you care most about views, snow, flowers, cost or crowds.
list: Mountain views: October to December, with January also excellent in Darjeeling.
Snow: January to March at Tsomgo, Zero Point and Sandakphu, accepting the risk of closed roads.
Rhododendrons: mid-April to May at Yumthang, on the Tsomgo road and on the Singalila ridge.
Gurudongmar Lake: April to June and October to November, when the road is most often open.
Toy train and tea: March to May and October to November, with spring for first-flush tea.
Lowest prices: August in Darjeeling, and January and February outside festival weeks.
Fewer crowds with good weather: March and November.

faqs.q: Which is the best month to visit Sikkim?
faqs.a: November is the best all-round month. Skies are very clear, roads are stable, North Sikkim is open and crowds are thinner than in October. October has equally good views but is the busiest month of the year because of the Puja holidays. For flowers rather than views, choose April or early May, and for snow choose January to March.

faqs.q: Can I visit Sikkim and Darjeeling in the monsoon?
faqs.a: You can, but plan carefully. From mid-June to September heavy rain causes landslides on NH10 and the hill roads, views are rare, and North Sikkim permits are often suspended. Darjeeling, Kalimpong and Gangtok towns remain open and are cheap and quiet. Keep spare days, avoid permit areas, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When will I see snow in Sikkim?
faqs.a: Snow is most reliable from December to March at Tsomgo Lake, Zero Point above Yumthang, and on the road to Nathu La, and Lachung village often gets snow from December to February. Gangtok and Darjeeling towns rarely see it. Heavy snow can close the high roads for days, so treat snow destinations as a bonus and keep a spare day.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see Kangchenjunga from Darjeeling?
faqs.a: October to January gives the best chance of clear views, with January often the clearest month of all and November close behind. Go to Tiger Hill or the Chowrasta ridge at dawn. In spring, views are good early in the morning but haze and cloud usually build by late morning. In the monsoon, clear views are rare.

faqs.q: Is May a good time for Sikkim?
faqs.a: May is pleasant, with warm days in Gangtok, peak rhododendrons at Yumthang and Gurudongmar usually open. It is also peak season for Indian school holidays, so hotels fill, Tsomgo is crowded and prices are at their highest. Book rooms and permits early. If you can travel in March or April instead, you get similar weather with fewer people.
